chapter: Teddy Wilson, Cafe Society and bebop
title: First hearing Dizzy Gillespie at the Cotton Club
summary: He first heard Dizzy sitting in with Cab's band in early 1939, trying something nobody understood.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Do you remember the first time you heard Dizzy Gillespie?
Cause he had been with Cab Calloway, too.
-- in and sat in with the band a couple of nights at the Cotton Club, that's the first time I heard him.
That was in -- must've been in '39, early '39, because I -- he took my place, in a way, either he or Mario Bauza, they both came in the same time.
At that time he was sounding like Roy Eldridge, wasn't he?
I think he did play that style, but when he was sitting in with us, he was fooling around with something else, nobody understood what he was doing, and everybody was giving him hell about it.
Well, he was always sort of a clown, but -- his personality was that way.
He was fooling around with something, a different style of trumpet at that time when he joined Cab. Nobody seemed to like it, they give him -- you know, talking about it, he was working on something.
I've heard it said that Cab Calloway once told him that he didn't want any Chinese music.
Well, that could be so, I don't know, I wouldn't be surprised at all.
